issue_decisions.finding: The One Time Settlement proposals dated 13th June, 2015 and 6th November, 2015 constitute a valid acknowledgment of liability under Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963, as they were in writing, signed by the Corporate Debtor, and made before the expiration of the original limitation period.
issue_decisions.application: Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963, states that an acknowledgment of liability in writing, signed by the party against whom the right is claimed, and made before the expiration of the prescribed period, computes a fresh period of limitation. The default occurred on 10th June, 2014 [F1], making the original three-year limitation period expire on 9th June, 2017. The One Time Settlement proposal dated 13th June, 2015 [F5, EX-1] and its reiteration on 6th November, 2015 [F6, EX-2] both occurred before this date. The content of EX-1, where the Corporate Debtor proposed 'settlement of its liabilities towards the lenders/financial creditors,' plainly indicates an acknowledgment of existing liabilities. Section 18 explicitly states that an acknowledgment is valid even if it 'omits to specify the exact nature of property/right' or 'is coupled with a claim to set off,' which covers the nature of a settlement proposal.
issue_decisions.conclusion: The One Time Settlement proposals effectively extended the period of limitation.

issue_decisions.finding: The application under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, filed on 19th September, 2018, is within the prescribed period of limitation due to the acknowledgment of liability.
issue_decisions.application: Given the finding on Issue I1, the latest acknowledgment of liability was made on 6th November, 2015 [F6]. According to Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963, a fresh period of limitation of three years is computed from this date. Therefore, the limitation period for filing the Section 7 application would expire on 5th November, 2018. The application under Section 7 was filed by Bank-Y on 19th September, 2018 [F2], which falls within this extended limitation period. The Adjudicating Authority's rejection based on the initial default date without considering the acknowledgment was therefore incorrect.
issue_decisions.conclusion: The Section 7 application is not barred by limitation.

opinions.overall_reasons: The Corporate Debtor's One Time Settlement proposals, dated 13th June, 2015 and 6th November, 2015, constitute a clear acknowledgment of liability under Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963. These acknowledgments were made in writing and before the expiry of the original limitation period, thereby extending the period of limitation. The latest acknowledgment on 6th November, 2015, reset the limitation clock, making the Section 7 application filed on 19th September, 2018, well within the three-year statutory period. Consequently, the Adjudicating Authority erred in rejecting the application as time-barred.
